walkthrough:
Write down the general term in the binomial expansion of $\left(2x + \frac{a}{x^2}\right)^5$:
$$T_{r+1} = \binom{5}{r}(2x)^{5-r}\left(\frac{a}{x^2}\right)^r = \binom{5}{r}2^{5-r}a^r x^{5-3r}$$

Set the power of $x$ equal to $-1$ to find the term in $\frac{1}{x}$:
$$5 - 3r = -1 \implies 3r = 6 \implies r = 2$$

Calculate the coefficient and equate it to $720$:
$$\binom{5}{2}2^{5-2}a^2 = 10(8)a^2 = 80a^2 = 720$$
$$a^2 = \frac{720}{80} = 9 \implies a = \pm 3$$

Set the power of $x$ equal to $-7$ to identify the term in $\frac{1}{x^7}$:
$$5 - 3r = -7 \implies 3r = 12 \implies r = 4$$
